title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: in the Teichmüller groupoid notes, G is a Mumford–Deligne ('MD') graph, i.e. a stable dual graph indexing a boundary stratum of M̄_{g,ν}. A is its set of edges and Â presumably the set of oriented edges or half-edges; this reading is not certain. For each vertex s, Â_s denotes the half-edges at s (internal edges plus marked legs). S_0T_G is the Teichmüller groupoid 'at infinity near the stratum G', with tangential base points. Each edge carries two symmetries: a Dehn twist, giving a factor Z, and an orientation flip, giving a factor μ_2.

Step 1. Special case: all vertices have genus 0 and index (valence) 3 or 4. The page gives
S_0T_G = (∏_{s∈S} S_0T_{0,Â_s}) ∧^{(Z^{Â_s},μ_2^{Â_s})} (Z^Â, μ_2^Â).
Each vertex groupoid S_0T_{0,Â_s} is a (Z^{Â_s}, μ_2^{Â_s})-groupoid: the twists around the boundary half-edges act centrally. The groupoid of G is the contracted product, i.e. the pushout, of the product of vertex groupoids along the map Z^{⊔Â_s} → Z^Â. This map identifies the twists of the two half-edges forming one internal edge. It is a gluing ('Lego') formula: the local Teichmüller groupoid near the stratum is built from the vertex pieces amalgamated over Dehn twists.

Step 2. Equivalently, there is a free (Z^Â, μ_2^Â)-groupoid with two quotients.
- Its quotient by (Z^I, μ_2^I) is S_0T_G. Here I is presumably the set of external legs or a sub-index set.
- Its quotient by all of (Z^Â, μ_2^Â) is the 'reduced' groupoid _∘R_0T_G = ∏_s _∘R_0T_{G_s^b} = ∏_s _∘T_{0,Â_s}.
Only index-4 vertices contribute, since M_{0,3} is a point. So the reduced object is a product of copies of the M_{0,4} (P^1 minus 3 points) fundamental groupoid with tangential base points.

Step 3. General MD graph G. S_0T_G is still a (Z^Â, μ_2^Â)-groupoid, μ_2^Â-free; the word 'libre' is crossed out in favour of 'μ_2^Â-free'. It is obtained as a filtered (finite) direct limit of such groupoids of the type in Steps 1–2.

Step 4. If G has virtual genus 0 on each connected component, the situation is 'rigid' (replacing the crossed-out 'limite'). The index category of the colimit can then be taken to be an ordered set: finite trees without index-2 vertices, of type G^b, i.e. with a chosen end on the π_0. The sentence breaks off.

Purpose: a local-to-global (two-level / 'Lego') presentation of the genus-0 Teichmüller tower near maximally degenerate points. This serves the Galois-action program of the Esquisse, by reducing to the index-4 genus-0 pieces. The next page passes to 'homomorphismes de généralisation' SP_G → SP_{G'}.
errors: No outright mathematical error is visible. The superscript in the contracted product is written ambiguously, sometimes μ_2^{Â} where μ_2^{Â_s} is meant. The meaning of I in (Z^I, μ_2^I) is not defined on the page.
The claim of μ_2^Â-freeness was corrected mid-writing from plain 'libre'. This suggests Grothendieck realized the Z^Â-action need not be free in general, e.g. for higher-genus vertices.
The final sentence on the index category is unfinished.

ideas.what: Gluing formula: local Teichmüller groupoid at a boundary stratum as contracted product (pushout over Dehn twist groups) of vertex groupoids
ideas.modern_name: Local fundamental group at the boundary of M̄_{g,n} / Lego–Teichmüller gluing; tangential base points at maximally degenerate curves
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse, 1984) as a program; worked out by Ihara–Nakamura, Nakamura, Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura–Schneps (1990s–2000)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (two-level principle, Lego-Teichmüller game) states the philosophy, not this formula

ideas.what: Dehn twists and edge orientation flips form a central (Z^Â, μ_2^Â) action; the quotient by it is the reduced groupoid, a product of M_{0,4} pieces
ideas.modern_name: Central extension by the Dehn twist lattice; reduction to genus-0, 4-point level

ideas.what: S_0T_G for arbitrary G is a filtered colimit of such groupoids; in the virtual genus 0 case the index category is a poset of reduced trees of type G^b
ideas.modern_name: Colimit / operadic presentation of genus-0 Teichmüller groupoids over trees (cf. parenthesized braids operad)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld, Bar-Natan, Tamarkin, Fresse (operadic genus-0 presentation)

missed.claim: The genus-0 Teichmüller groupoid at infinity is presented as a filtered colimit, indexed by a poset of reduced trees, of free (Z^Â, μ_2^Â)-groupoids built from M_{0,4} pieces. This anticipates the operadic, tree-indexed description of genus-0 braid groupoids (parenthesized braids) used for GT. The explicit μ_2 orientation-flip bookkeeping is not usually present in that literature.
missed.quote: S_0T_G (G graphe MD quelconque) est un (Z^Â,μ_2^Â)-groupoïde μ_2^Â-libre comme Lim (fini) de (Z^Â,μ_2^Â)-groupoïdes
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mostly of historical interest; it is an early, pre-Drinfeld formulation of the tree-colimit picture. Its likely date is around 1978–84.

deep.surprise_reason: This is consistent with the Esquisse's announced two-level/Lego principle, which was later developed in detail by Nakamura, Schneps, Lochak and others. The tree-poset colimit with μ_2-twisting is a nice unpublished detail, but not a new result.
